Start with a goal notebook from [Choose a simulation](../start/choose-a-simulation.qmd#getting-started), then use the topic links below to find the model, geometry, mesh, execution or result guidance for that task. Check [Terms and units](terms-and-units.qmd) when a technical term or unit needs clarification.

## Model and materials {#model-materials}

Start with the [physical problem](../concepts/problems.qmd) and
[model assumptions](../concepts/model-and-numerics.qmd#define-the-physical-model).
The [physical representation contract](specs/physical-representation.qmd#typed-source-carrier-and-plan)
describes how source declarations reach backend preparation.

## Conductors and ports {#conductors-ports}

Read [Entities, occurrences, and Nets](../concepts/geometry.qmd#entity-occurrence-and-net)
with the [driven-response concept](../concepts/problems.qmd#driven-response-excite-a-port-at-a-frequency).
The [model preparation tutorial](../guides/prepare-a-layout.qmd) shows how those
choices enter a selected case; the [Driven Terminal](../guides/s-parameters-hfss.qmd)
lesson shows the lumped-port declarations. Driven Modal and wave ports are not
available in this version.

## Mesh and adaptation {#mesh-adaptation}

The [mesh quality contract](specs/mesh-quality.qmd#audit) defines
what `mesh()` audits and records about each mesh. The [prepared-backend tutorial](../guides/inspect-the-prepared-model.qmd)
shows where to inspect the mesh and native preparation before execution.

## Execution and handoff {#execution-handoff}

Use the [execution profile contract](specs/execution-profiles.qmd#handoff-lifecycle)
for portable handoffs and caller-controlled solver runs, then follow the
[handoff tutorial](../guides/run-elsewhere.qmd).

## Results and reports {#results-reports}

The [report contract](specs/report-model.qmd#common-envelope) describes result
identity, availability, and presentation. The
[returned-results tutorial](../guides/convergence-and-reports.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use)
shows how to read a completed run folder for a selected use.

## Saved fields and offline loss {#saved-fields-offline-loss}

Use the [saved-field tutorial](../guides/saved-fields.qmd#recover-the-exact-prepared-model)
for native field evaluation and the [offline EPR tutorial](../guides/offline-loss.qmd#interpret-an-assumption-change)
for assumption changes on recorded results.
`analyze_epr` evaluates retained saved fields through native AEDT and needs an
explicitly selected AEDT release and its license; `reanalyze_epr` updates the
assumptions of a resolved EPR result offline. The
[analyze_epr reference](api/analyze-epr.qmd) gives its parameters and
signature.

## Find the right reference {#find-the-right-reference}

| Need | Start here |
|---|---|
| Check which solver workflows SCGSim supports | [Supported calculations](supported-calculations.qmd) |
| Prepare, seal and evaluate saved AEDT fields | [AEDT: analyze saved fields](../guides/saved-fields.qmd) |

| Look up the parameters and signature of `analyze_epr` | [analyze_epr](api/analyze-epr.qmd) |
| Browse the declared public names of each package | [API index](api-index.qmd) |
| Review source ownership and API boundaries | [Architecture](../contribute/architecture.qmd) |

## Junction capacitance reference {#junction-capacitance-reference}

For one junction in a given mode and pass, $V$ is its complex peak-phasor voltage and $U_{norm}$ is the electric-energy normalization, not total electric-plus-magnetic energy. For nonzero $V$, the effective modal capacitance is $C_{mode}=2U_{norm}/|V|^2$, the branch capacitance is $C_j=2U_{C,j}/|V|^2$, and the participation ratio is $p_{C,j}=C_j/C_{mode}$. At $V=0$, the ratio is undefined. The [AEDT runtime contract](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#surface-estimates-and-junction-normalization) records the full voltage, energy and normalization definitions.
